ops.title: Drive lock deleted: one write primitive (long-running 1.0.1649)
ops.body: Before (2026-11-16 00:11–01:45): every drive writer loaded and saved the whole drive under the drive's `.lock`, and ~200 sites wrote through four scattered APIs (`edit`, `update`, `after_save`, `batch`) plus ~12 hand-rolled pid claims. writes.log showed about 86 whole-drive writes a minute, and one ten-minute window had 203 s held and 143 s waited. After (1.0.1649, 645ff878a): every write goes through `state.write(name, change, *, budget, patient)`. It commits the rows it changed by compare-and-set inside one sqlite `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, and on a race it re-runs the change with backoff until its budget runs out, then refuses. Watch stages get `WATCH_WRITE_SECONDS` and skip to the next pass. Writes that record an outside action already done (a post, launch, merge or card) are `patient` and never skip. Effects run once after the commit via `state.after`. Child processes start under reservations (`reserve`/`adopt`/`settle`/`cancel`/`holder`, liveness by pid plus birth time, children pass `--reserved`). Lane replies go through a durable job outbox (`owe_reply`, replayed each watch pass). The `.lock`/`.first.lock`, `locked`/`writing`/`handled_lock` and the old APIs are gone. reloads.json and the watch pid file have their own flocks. In writes.log, 08:59–09:10 showed 602 row commits with 1.6 s held and 0.3 s waited, and 1.0.1649 itself took zero whole-drive holds. Old `drive mcp` servers and hooks exec the newest installed drive on each call, so they never used the old lock. Designs and reviews: write-primitive-design.md, result-primitive.md, result-sites.md, result-reds.md and result-delete.md, all under the lane's scratch folder.
